# Derived geometric Satake for $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}}$ Thanks: Part of this work was done when the author was supported by NSF DGE-2140743

**Authors:** S. K. Devalapurkar Address: 1 Oxford St, Cambridge, MA 02139 Email address: sdevalapurkar@math.harvard.edu, August 24, 2026

## Abstract

In this note, we study the local relative geometric Langlands conjecture of Ben-Zvi–Sakellaridis–Venkatesh for the spherical subgroup $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}}$ of the triple product $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ (and also for the spherical subgroup $\mathrm{G}_{2}$ of $\mathrm{SO}_{8}/\mu_{2}$ ), whose corresponding Langlands dual $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ -variety can be identified with the symplectic vector space $(\mathbf{A}^{2})^{\otimes 3}\cong\mathbf{A}^{8}$ of $2\times 2\times 2$ -cubes. Our analysis relies on a construction of Bhargava relating $2\times 2\times 2$ -cubes to Gauss composition on quadratic forms, arising here as the moment map for the Hamiltonian $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ -action on $(\mathbf{A}^{2})^{\otimes 3}$ , and the Cayley hyperdeterminant as studied by Gelfand-Kapranov-Zelevinsky.

#### Contents

- 1 Introduction

- 2 Some properties of $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$

- 3 The proof, and some remarks

- 4 Variants

## 1. Introduction

The goal of this brief note is to study the geometrization of a story from the arithmetic context pioneered by Böcherer, Gross, Harris, Ichino, Kudla, Prasad, Schulze-Pillot, and Watson, among many others (see, e.g., [HK, Ich, Pra, Wat]): this tale is about the “triple product period”. In the language of geometric representation theory, our goal is to study derived geometric Satake ([BZSV, Conjecture 7.5.1]) for the spherical $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ -variety $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}}$ . This is a natural generalization of the “group case”, i.e., derived geometric Satake for the spherical $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 2}$ -variety $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 2}/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}}$ (which amounts simply to the derived geometric Satake equivalence of [BF] for $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ ). Similar methods allow us to analyze the spherical $\mathrm{PSO}_{8}$ -variety $\mathrm{PSO}_{8}/\mathrm{G}_{2}$ , too. In order to state our main result, some notation is necessary.

#### Notation 1.1.

Let $\mathrm{std}$ denote the standard representation of $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ , so that $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$ consists of cubes

$$ \textstyle{b_{2}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{d_{3}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{a\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{b_{1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{d_{1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{c.} \textstyle{b_{3}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{d_{2}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} $$

Fix an integer $n$ . Equip $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$ with the grading where the entries of a cube have the following weights: $a$ lives in weight $-4n$ , each $b_{i}$ lives in weight $-2n$ , $c$ lives in weight $2n$ , and each $d_{i}$ lives in weight $0$ . Write $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}(4n,\vec{2n},-2n,\vec{0})$ to denote the corresponding graded variety.

Similarly, equip $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ with the grading where the entries of a matrix $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ c&d\end{pmatrix}$ have the following weights: $a$ and $d$ live in weight $0$ , $b$ lives in weight $2n$ , and $c$ lives in weight $-2n$ . Write $\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-2n\rho)$ to denote this graded group. Then there is a natural graded action of $\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-2n\rho)^{\times 3}$ on $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}(4n,\vec{2n},-2n,\vec{0})$ .

Recall that the process of shearing (denoted $\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}$ ) discussed in [Rak, Lur], as well as [Dev, Section 2.1], converts gradings into homological shifts (more precisely, it sends a module in weight $n$ to the same module shifted homologically by $n$ ). This functor is symmetric monoidal when restricted to the subcategory of modules in even weights, and therefore extends to an operation on evenly graded stacks. If $Y$ is a graded stack, let $\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}Y$ denote the corresponding derived stack obtained by shearing, and let $\mathrm{Perf}^{\mathrm{sh}}(Y)$ denote $\mathrm{Perf}(\mathrm{sh}^{1/2}Y)$ . Almost all of our discussion below takes place in the setting of ordinary, and not derived, algebraic geometry, and so the reader unfamiliar with derived algebraic geometry should feel free to ignore this procedure of shearing.11 1 The reader intent on ignoring shearing might feel some solace in noting that our main results should continue to hold with the $\infty$ -category of constructible sheaves replaced by a mixed variant. However, this must (hopefully temporarily) be regarded as a reverie, since no “mixed” version of the derived geometric Satake equivalence seems to exist in the literature.

As in [Dev], we will state all of our results with “arithmetic shearing” in the sense of [BZSV, Section 6.7]. The following result concerns [BZSV, Conjecture 7.5.1] for the Hamiltonian $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ -variety $T^{\ast}(\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}})$ and the Hamiltonian $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ -variety $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$ .

#### Theorem 1.2 (Derived geometric Satake for $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}}$ ).

Suppose that the $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}[\![t]\!]$ -action on $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}}(\!(t)\!)$ is optimal in the sense of [Dev, Hypothesis 3.5.2]. There is an equivalence22 2 The $\infty$ -category on the left-hand side is as in [Dev, Definition 3.6.1]; see Definition 3.1 for a quick review.

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}}(\!(t)\!));\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}^{\mathrm{sh}}(\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}(4,\vec{2},-2,\vec{0})/\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-2\rho)^{\times 3}). $$

Moreover, this equivalence is equivariant for the action of the spherical Hecke category for $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ ; on the spectral side, this action is encoded by Bhargava’s construction $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}\to\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast,\times 3}$ of three quadratic forms from a point of $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$ (see [Bha1, Woo]).

#### Remark 1.3.

The hypothesis of optimality in Theorem 1.2 is equivalent to the hypothesis that the diagonal action of $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}[\![t]\!]$ on $\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}}\times\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}}$ is optimal, where $\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}}$ is the affine Grassmannian of $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ . In particular, [Dev, Hypothesis 3.5.2(a) and (b)] can be deduced from this observation. Checking purity of the $\mathrm{IC}$ -sheaves seems a bit trickier, but should not be difficult.

#### Remark 1.4.

Let $\mathrm{PSO}_{2n}:=\mathrm{SO}_{2n}/\mu_{2}$ . Then, the embedding $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}}\subseteq\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ can be identified with the diagonal embedding $\mathrm{SO}_{3}\subseteq\mathrm{SO}_{3}\times\mathrm{PSO}_{4}$ ; and similarly, the action of $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ on $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$ can be identified with the action of $\mathrm{Spin}_{4}\times\mathrm{Sp}_{2}$ on the tensor product of their respective defining representations. From this perspective, Theorem 1.2 could be viewed as a special case of the geometrized analogue of the Gan-Gross-Prasad period (or at least a period isogenous to it). See Remark 3.12 (as well as [Dev, Example 3.6.24]) for a discussion of the Gan-Gross-Prasad period along the lines of this article.

See Remark 3.10 for an analogue of Theorem 1.2 for the non-spherical variety $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 4}/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}}$ .

An argument similar to that of Theorem 1.2 shows a variant for $\mathrm{PSO}_{8}$ . (The arithmetic version of the result stated below was studied, for instance, in [Jia2, Jia3].) Namely, there is an embedding $\mathrm{G}_{2}\subseteq\mathrm{PSO}_{8}$ given by triality, which exhibits $\mathrm{G}_{2}$ as a spherical subgroup of $\mathrm{PSO}_{8}$ . To see that this situation is analogous to that of Theorem 1.2, note that the Dynkin diagram $\bullet$ of $A_{1}$ is obtained from the Dynkin diagram $\bullet\bullet\bullet$ of $A_{1}^{\times 3}$ by folding with respect to the obvious action of the symmetric group $\Sigma_{3}$ . In the same way, the Dynkin diagram of $\mathrm{G}_{2}$ is obtained from the Dynkin diagram of $D_{4}$ by folding with respect to the action of $\Sigma_{3}$ permuting the three vertices around the branching vertex. The following result concerns [BZSV, Conjecture 7.5.1] for the Hamiltonian $\mathrm{PSO}_{8}$ -variety $T^{\ast}(\mathrm{PSO}_{8}/\mathrm{G}_{2})$ and the Hamiltonian $\mathrm{Spin}_{8}$ -variety $\mathrm{Ind}_{\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}}^{\mathrm{Spin}_{8}}(\mathbf{A}^{1}\oplus\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3})$ .

#### Theorem 1.5 (Derived geometric Satake for $\mathrm{PSO}_{8}/\mathrm{G}_{2}$ ).

Suppose that the $\mathrm{PSO}_{8}[\![t]\!]$ -action on $\mathrm{PSO}_{8}(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{G}_{2}(\!(t)\!)$ is optimal in the sense of [Dev, Hypothesis 3.5.2]. Then there is an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{PSO}_{8}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{PSO}_{8}(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{G}_{2}(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}^{\mathrm{sh}}(\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}(12,\vec{6},-6,\vec{0})/\mathrm{SL}_{2}(-6\rho)^{\times 3}\times\mathbf{A}^{1}(4)). $$

This implies, for instance, that the spherical subgroups $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 2}\subseteq\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 4}$ (given by $(g,h)\mapsto(g,g,g,h)$ ) and $\mathrm{G}_{2}\subseteq\mathrm{PSO}_{8}$ have the same dual quotient stacks (namely, $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}/\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}\times\mathbf{A}^{1}$ ) up to grading. Therefore, they fit into the paradigm of [Dev, Remark 4.1.5].

The proofs of Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.5 reduce to showing that the conditions of [Dev, Theorem 3.6.4] are met. This ultimately relies on studying Bhargava’s construction from [Bha1] relating $2\times 2\times 2$ -matrices to quadratic forms, and the work [GKZ] of Gelfand-Kapranov-Zelevinsky describing the relationship to Cayley’s hyperdeterminant. The work presented in this article indicates that there is much more to explore regarding the relationship between (relative) geometric Langlands (following [BZSV]), prehomogeneous vector spaces (following [SK]), and the progress in arithmetic invariant theory (using the terminology of [BG]) over the past 20 years spurred by Bhargava’s thesis. To illustrate this, here are two concrete questions in the interface of these subjects:

- • Can one use Bhargava’s work [Bha1] on the $\mathrm{SL}_{6}(\mathbf{Z})$ -action on $\wedge^{3}\mathbf{Z}^{6}$ to approach the geometrized version of [GR1] (i.e., [BZSV, Line 16 of Table 1.5.1])? (Here, the information flows from arithmetic invariant theory to relative geometric Langlands.)

- • Following the work of Moore and Tachikawa in [MT], let $\overline{\mathcal{O}}:=\overline{\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{min}}}(\mathfrak{so}_{8})$ denote the minimal nilpotent coadjoint orbit of $\mathfrak{so}_{8}$ , so that it is $10$ -dimensional. It has a canonical action of $\mathrm{SO}_{8}$ , and hence a canonical action of $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 4}\subseteq\mathrm{SO}_{8}$ . In fact, more is true: there is an action of the symmetric group $\Sigma_{4}$ on $\mathfrak{so}_{8}$ extending the $\Sigma_{3}\subseteq\Sigma_{4}$ -action by triality, whose fixed subgroup is $\mathfrak{sl}_{3}\subseteq\mathfrak{g}_{2}$ . (See [FJLS, Section 4.1] for a description of this action.) This defines an action of $\Sigma_{4}$ on $\overline{\mathcal{O}}$ , and in fact the action of $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 4}$ on $\overline{\mathcal{O}}$ is $\Sigma_{4}$ -equivariant for the permutation action on $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 4}$ . The action $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 4}\circlearrowleft\overline{\mathcal{O}}$ should be viewed as the analogue of $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}\circlearrowleft(\mathbf{A}^{2})^{\otimes 3}$ ; see also Remark 3.10.33 3 Here is another (related) reason. As described in [Dev, Remark 3.6.25], both of these examples can be placed in the following context. The groups $(\mathrm{SL}_{2},\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 2})$ form a reductive dual pair in $\mathrm{Sp}_{8}$ , and $(\mathbf{A}^{2})^{\otimes 3}$ is a double cover of the minimal nilpotent orbit closure of $\mathrm{Sp}_{8}$ . Similarly, the groups $(\mathrm{SL}_{2},\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3})$ form a reductive dual pair in $\mathrm{SO}_{8}$ , and $\overline{\mathcal{O}}$ is the minimal nilpotent orbit closure of $\mathrm{SO}_{8}$ . One should therefore view these examples as falling under the purview of Howe duality. There is a map $\overline{\mathcal{O}}\to\mathbf{A}^{1}$ , which we will call the “discriminant”, which defines an isomorphism

$$ \overline{\mathcal{O}}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 4}\xrightarrow{{\sim}}\mathbf{A}^{1}, $$

at least over $\mathbf{C}$ . The above isomorphism should also hold true over $\mathbf{Z}$ . Following [Bha1], let us introduce some terminology. An ordered tuple $(I_{1},I_{2},I_{3},I_{4})$ of oriented ideals of a quadratic ring $S$ such that $I_{1}I_{2}I_{3}I_{4}\subseteq S$ and $N(I_{1})N(I_{2})N(I_{3})N(I_{4})=1$ will be called balanced, and say that two such balanced tuples $(I_{1},I_{2},I_{3},I_{4})$ and $(I_{1}^{\prime},I_{2}^{\prime},I_{3}^{\prime},I_{4}^{\prime})$ are equivalent if there are elements $x_{1},\cdots,x_{4}\in S\otimes\mathbf{Q}$ such that $I_{j}^{\prime}=x_{j}I_{j}$ . Say that an $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 4}(\mathbf{Z})$ -orbit on $\overline{\mathcal{O}}(\mathbf{Z})$ is nondegenerate if its discriminant is nonzero. Then, one should have the following analogue of [Bha1, Theorem 11]: Conjecture 1.6. There is a canonical bijection between the set of nondegenerate $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 4}(\mathbf{Z})$ -orbits on $\overline{\mathcal{O}}(\mathbf{Z})$ and the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(S,(I_{1},I_{2},I_{3},I_{4}))$ of a nondegenerate oriented quadratic ring $S$ and an equivalence class $(I_{1},I_{2},I_{3},I_{4})$ of balanced oriented ideals of $S$ . If this were true, one could symmetrize, i.e., take $I_{1}=I_{2}=I_{3}=I_{4}$ , so that $I:=I_{1}$ will be a $4$ -torsion element in the class group of $S$ . It would be very interesting if one could use the explicit description of the invariant quotient $\overline{\mathcal{O}}/\!\!/\Sigma_{4}$ in [FJLS, Theorem 4.6 and Theorem 4.12] to describe the asymptotics of $4$ -torsion in class groups of quadratic rings over $\mathbf{Z}$ . (Here, the information flows from relative geometric Langlands to arithmetic invariant theory.)

In Remark 2.14 and Remark 4.14, I have included some further natural observations/questions whose role in the picture of geometric Langlands is unclear to me, in the hopes that it will stimulate further investigation into these questions.

#### Remark 1.7.

The arguments of this article should continue to hold if one considers sheaves with coefficients in $\mathbf{Z}[\frac{1}{2}]$ ; we have not checked this explicitly, but it seems likely to be true. In fact, we expect that the results of this article should continue to hold for sheaves with coefficients in $\mathbf{Z}$ itself. This, however, is a rather more subtle question: the prime $2$ is an interesting one (see Remark 2.8).

More generally, following the philosophy of [Dev], it should also be possible to use a variant of the methods of this article to prove analogues of Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.5 for sheaves with coefficients in connective complex K-theory $\mathrm{ku}$ . We have not attempted to do this, but we expect the corresponding $1$ -parameter deformation of $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$ over $\pi_{\ast}(\mathrm{ku})\cong\mathbf{Z}[\beta]$ to be a rather interesting $\mathrm{ku}$ -Hamiltonian $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ -variety.

#### Remark 1.8.

The equivalence of Theorem 1.2 can heuristically be viewed as geometric Langlands for $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ on the “doubled raviolo”, obtained by gluing three formal disks along their common punctured disk. I expect Theorem 1.2 to be related to the work of [MT], and hope to address this relationship and the context of Theorem 1.2 in physics in joint work with Ben-Zvi and Gunningham.

Theorem 1.2 is also related to the monoidality of the derived Satake equivalence. The $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}}(\!(t)\!));\mathbf{Q})$ can be identified with $\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}}\times\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}};\mathbf{Q})$ , where $\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}}$ is the affine Grassmannian of $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ . In particular, it can be used to describe the ordinary tensor product on $\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}};\mathbf{Q})$ . Theorem 1.2 says that under the derived geometric Satake equivalence of [BF] identifying this $\infty$ -category with $\mathrm{Perf}^{\mathrm{sh}}(\Sym^{2}(\mathrm{std})/\mathrm{SL}_{2})$ , the ordinary tensor product on $\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}};\mathbf{Q})$ can be identified with Gauss composition of binary quadratic forms (in the way described by Bhargava), i.e., via the correspondence 2.44 4 This is similar to how the convolution tensor product on $\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathrm{PGL}_{2}};\mathbf{Q})$ can be identified with the usual tensor product on $\mathrm{Perf}^{\mathrm{sh}}(\Sym^{2}(\mathrm{std})/\mathrm{SL}_{2})$ . (In fact, I learned after writing this article that the main calculation of this article also appears in [BFN, Section 5(iii)]. The approach taken here is somewhat different, in that the calculations are more explicit and fit into the story of [Dev]; I hope that the reader might find this alternative perspective useful.)

In the final section of this article, we suggest some variants of Theorem 1.2 with $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ replaced by variants. Namely, we expect:

- • Let $G=\mathrm{Res}_{\mathbf{C}[\![t^{1/3}]\!]/\mathbf{C}[\![t]\!]}\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ , where $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ is viewed as a constant group scheme over $\mathbf{C}[\![t^{1/3}]\!]$ . Then there should be a fully faithful functor from the $\infty$ -category of perfect complexes on a shearing of the quotient stack $\Sym^{3}(\mathrm{std})/\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ to $\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(G(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})$ . The grading with respect to which the shearing is taken is described in Conjecture 4.7.

- • Let $G=\mathrm{Res}_{(\mathbf{C}[\![t^{1/2}]\!]\times\mathbf{C}[\![t]\!])/\mathbf{C}[\![t]\!]}\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ . Then there should be a fully faithful functor from the $\infty$ -category of perfect complexes on a shearing of the quotient stack $(\mathrm{std}\otimes\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast})/\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 2}$ to $\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(G(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})$ . The grading with respect to which the shearing is taken is described in Conjecture 4.11.

#### Remark 1.9.

The quotient stack $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}/\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ is also studied (in different language, of course) in quantum information theory; see Remark 2.11 below.

Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.5 are predicted by (the Betti version of) the local geometric conjecture of Ben-Zvi–Sakellaridis–Venkatesh; see [BZSV, Conjecture 7.5.1]. My homotopy-theoretic interpretation of their conjecture is as follows. Suppose $G$ is a reductive group over $\mathbf{C}$ and $G/H$ is an affine homogeneous spherical $G$ -variety (meaning that it admits an open $B$ -orbit for its natural left $B\subseteq G$ -action). Then, there should be a dual graded ${\check{{G}}}$ -variety ${\check{{M}}}$ equipped with a moment map $\mu:{\check{{M}}}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ , and an equivalence of the form

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c,\mathrm{Sat}}(G(\!(t)\!)/H(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{C})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}^{\mathrm{sh}}({\check{{M}}}/{\check{{G}}}), $$

where $\mathrm{Perf}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ denotes the $\infty$ -category of perfect complexes on the shearing of ${\check{{M}}}/{\check{{G}}}$ with respect to its given grading. In fact, [BZSV, Section 4] gives an explicit construction of this predicted dual ${\check{{M}}}$ , and in the examples $(G,H)=(\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\times 3},\mathrm{PGL}_{2}^{\mathrm{diag}})$ and $(\mathrm{PSO}_{8},\mathrm{G}_{2})$ , one can compute that the stacky quotient ${\check{{M}}}/{\check{{G}}}$ is isomorphic to the right-hand sides of Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.5 respectively.55 5 In the first case, this computation is straightforward given the prescription of [BZSV, Section 4]; see [Sak, Example 7.2.4] for a reference. The computation in the second case goes as follows. As in [BZSV, Remark 7.1.1], the quotient stack ${\check{{M}}}/{\check{{G}}}$ can be identified with the quotient ${\check{{V}}}_{X}/{\check{{G}}}_{X}$ , where ${\check{{G}}}_{X}$ is the Gaitsgory-Nadler/Sakellaridis-Venkatesh/Knop-Schalke dual group of $X$ and ${\check{{V}}}_{X}$ is constructed in [BZSV, Section 4.5]. In the case $X=\mathrm{PSO}_{8}/\mathrm{G}_{2}$ , a calculation shows that ${\check{{G}}}_{X}$ is the Levi subgroup of the maximal parabolic subgroup of $\mathrm{PSO}_{8}$ corresponding to the central vertex of the $D_{4}$ Dynkin diagram; so ${\check{{G}}}_{X}\cong\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ . Using the prescription of [BZSV, Section 4.5], one can check that ${\check{{V}}}_{X}\cong\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}\oplus\mathbf{A}^{1}$ , where ${\check{{G}}}_{X}$ acts only on the first factor. See, e.g., [Sak, Line 9 of Table in Appendix A].

Lest Theorem 1.2 seem like an oddly specific example to focus on, we note that it is essentially the only “new” example of a spherical pair $(G,H)$ of the form $(H^{\times j},H^{\mathrm{diag}})$ , as shown by the following lemma.

#### Lemma 1.10.

Suppose $H$ is a simple linear algebraic group over $\mathbf{C}$ . Then the subgroup $H^{\mathrm{diag}}\subseteq H^{\times j}$ is spherical if and only if:

- (a) $j=2$ , and $H$ arbitrary;

- (b) $j=3$ and $H$ is of type $A_{1}$ .

#### Proof.

If the subgroup $H^{\mathrm{diag}}\subseteq H^{\times j}$ is spherical, there is an open $H^{\mathrm{diag}}$ -orbit on the flag variety of $H^{\times j}$ . This implies that the dimension of $H$ must be at least $j|\Phi^{+}|$ , where $\Phi^{+}$ is the set of positive roots; equivalently, one needs $\mathrm{rank}(H)\geq(j-2)|\Phi^{+}|$ . Of course, this is always satisfied if $j=2$ (this is the group case corresponding to the symmetric subgroup $H^{\mathrm{diag}}\subseteq H\times H$ ). Using the classification of simple linear algebraic groups over $\mathbf{C}$ , it is easy to see that the only other case when the above inequality can hold is when $j=3$ and $H$ is of type $A_{1}$ ; one can then check by hand that the diagonal subgroup in this case is indeed spherical. ∎

In the first case of Lemma 1.10, [BZSV, Conjecture 7.5.1] is precisely the derived geometric Satake equivalence of [BF]. Therefore, the only other case of Lemma 1.10 is when $H$ is simple of type $A_{1}$ , and Theorem 1.2 precisely addresses [BZSV, Conjecture 7.5.1] for the adjoint form $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ of $H$ .

## 2. Some properties of $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$

In this section, we establish some basic properties of $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$ as a $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ -variety; our base field will always be $\mathbf{Q}$ , and we will write ${\check{{G}}}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ . Some of this material appears in [Bha1, Woo]. In particular, Construction 2.3 is due to Bhargava.

#### Observation 2.1.

An element $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ c&-a\end{pmatrix}\in\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}\cong\mathfrak{sl}_{2}$ can be identified with a binary quadratic form $q_{A}(x,y)=cx^{2}+2axy-by^{2}$ . The resulting identification between $\Sym^{2}(\mathrm{std})=(\mathrm{std}\otimes\mathrm{std})_{\Sigma_{2}}$ and $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}$ is $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ -equivariant. Note, moreover, that the discriminant of $q_{A}(x,y)$ is $-4\mathrm{det}(A)$ .

#### Warning 2.2.

Note that under Observation 2.1, the element of $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}$ associated to a binary quadratic form $bx^{2}+axy+cy^{2}$ is not the symmetric matrix associated to the quadratic form! Indeed, the associated symmetric matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}b&a/2\\ a/2&c\end{pmatrix}$ , while the associated element of $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}$ is $\begin{pmatrix}a/2&c\\ b&-a/2\end{pmatrix}$ .

Note, also, that we are relying quite heavily on the assumption that $2$ is invertible in $\mathbf{Q}$ . Over $\mathbf{Z}$ , one can in fact identify the space $(\mathbf{A}^{2}\otimes\mathbf{A}^{2})_{\Sigma_{2}}$ of binary quadratic forms with the coadjoint representation $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}\cong\mathfrak{pgl}_{2}$ of $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ . Working over $\mathbf{Z}$ and keeping track of the difference between $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}$ and $\mathfrak{pgl}_{2}$ has the effect of eliminating extraneous factors of $2$ in our discussion below; but working over $\mathbf{Z}$ also introduces new complications (see Remark 2.8) which we do not wish to address in the present article.

#### Construction 2.3.

The affine space $\mathbf{A}^{8}=\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$ can be regarded as parametrizing cubes

Indeed, removing the vertex in the Dynkin diagram of type $\mathrm{D}_{j+2}$ which is connected to the affine root in the extended Dynkin diagram defines a maximal parabolic subgroup $P$ of $\mathrm{SO}_{2j+2}$ , and its Levi quotient $L$ is $\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times\mathrm{SO}_{2j}$ . (When this procedure is applied to the Dynkin diagram of a general semisimple $G$ , the resulting Levi subgroup is the centralizer of the $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ embedded in $G$ via the highest root of $\mathfrak{g}$ .) If $U$ denotes the unipotent radical of $P$ , then $L$ acts on the vector space $U/[U,U]$ by conjugation, and the Lie bracket on $U$ defines a symplectic form on $U/[U,U]$ . With a bit of pain, one can check that $U/[U,U]\cong\mathrm{std}\otimes\mathrm{std}_{2j}$ as a symplectic $L\cong\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times\mathrm{SO}_{2j}$ -representation.

The same construction with the Dynkin diagram of type $\mathrm{B}_{j+2}$ produces $\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times\mathrm{SO}_{2j+1}$ acting on $\mathrm{std}\otimes\mathrm{std}_{2j+1}$ . Doing this procedure for the other Dynkin diagrams produces some of the “vectorial” examples in one of the columns in [BZSV, Table 1.5.1]. For example, the type $\mathrm{A}_{n+1}$ Dynkin diagram produces $\mathrm{GL}_{n}$ acting on $T^{\ast}(\mathrm{std}_{n})$ , and I believe the Dynkin diagram for $\mathrm{E}_{6}$ will produce $\mathrm{SL}_{6}$ acting on $\wedge^{3}\mathrm{std}_{6}$ . One also obtains some representations not included by [BZSV]; for instance, the Dynkin diagram of $\mathrm{G}_{2}$ will produce $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ acting on $\Sym^{3}(\mathrm{std})$ , which is not “hyperspherical” (see [BZSV, Example 5.1.10]). For this last calculation, see [Spr, Pages 160-161]. I do not yet understand the significance of these observations in the context of relative geometric Langlands.

This leads us to the main calculation. It implies, for instance, that the stabilizer (inside $\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ ) of a element of $\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$ with nonvanishing Cayley hyperdeterminant can be identified with $\mathbf{G}_{m}^{2}\cong\ker(\mathbf{G}_{m}^{3}\xrightarrow{{\text{prod}}}\mathbf{G}_{m})$ .

#### Proposition 2.15.

Let ${\check{{J}}}$ denote the group scheme over $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}\cong\spec\mathbf{Q}[a^{2}]$ of regular centralizers for $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ , so that

$$ \displaystyle{\check{{J}}} \displaystyle\cong\spec\mathbf{Q}[a,\alpha^{\pm 1},\tfrac{\alpha-\alpha^{-1}}{a}]^{\mathbf{Z}/2}\cong\spec\mathbf{Q}[a^{2},\alpha+\alpha^{-1},\tfrac{\alpha-\alpha^{-1}}{a}] \displaystyle\cong\ker(\mathrm{Res}_{\mathbf{Q}[a]/\mathbf{Q}[a^{2}]}\mathbf{G}_{m}\xrightarrow{{\mathrm{Nm}}}\mathbf{G}_{m}), $$

where the action of $\mathbf{Z}/2$ sends $a\mapsto-a$ and $\alpha\mapsto\alpha^{-1}$ , and the group structure is such that $\alpha$ is grouplike. Then there is an isomorphism

$$ \mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times_{\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}/{\check{{G}}}}\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}\cong\ker({\check{{J}}}\times_{\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}}{\check{{J}}}\times_{\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}}{\check{{J}}}\xrightarrow{{\mathrm{prod}}}{\check{{J}}}) $$

#### Proof.

The fiber product on the left identifies with the subgroup of $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times{\check{{G}}}$ of those $(a^{2},\vec{g})$ such that $\vec{g}=(g_{1},g_{2},g_{3})\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ stabilizes $\kappa(a^{2})$ . The trick to determining this stabilizer is to use Bhargava’s construction from Construction 2.3: if $\vec{g}$ stabilizes a cube $\mathcal{C}$ , it must also stabilize the corresponding triple $\mu(\mathcal{C})\in\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast,\times 3}$ of quadratic forms.

First, a simple calculation shows that if $a$ is a unit, the triple of matrices

$$ \vec{g}=\left(\begin{pmatrix}-1&a^{-1}\\
a&1\end{pmatrix},\begin{pmatrix}-1&a^{-1}\\
a&1\end{pmatrix},\begin{pmatrix}-1&a^{-1}\\
a&1\end{pmatrix}\right)\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3} $$

sends

$$ \kappa(a^{2})\mapsto-4(a^{2},\vec{0},a^{-1},\vec{0}). $$

The triple $\vec{g}$ can be thought of as “diagonalizing” $\kappa(a^{2})$ . The stabilizer of the cube $-4(a^{2},\vec{0},a^{-1},\vec{0})$ precisely consists of triples of matrices of the form

$$ \left(\begin{pmatrix}\alpha_{1}&0\\
0&\alpha_{1}^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\begin{pmatrix}\alpha_{2}&0\\
0&\alpha_{2}^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\begin{pmatrix}\alpha_{3}&0\\
0&\alpha_{3}^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\right)\text{ with }\alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}\alpha_{3}=1. $$

For $\alpha\in\mathbf{G}_{m}$ , let $h(\alpha)$ denote the matrix

$$ h(\alpha)=\frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}\alpha+\alpha^{-1}&\frac{\alpha^{-1}-\alpha}{a}\\
a^{2}\cdot\frac{\alpha^{-1}-\alpha}{a}&\alpha+\alpha^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}. $$

Conjugating 3 by the element $\vec{g}\in{\check{{G}}}$ , we find that the triple $(h(\alpha_{1}),h(\alpha_{2}),h(\alpha_{3}))$ of matrices stabilizes $\kappa(a^{2})$ as long as $\alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}\alpha_{3}=1$ and $a^{2}\in\mathbf{G}_{m}\subseteq\mathbf{A}^{1}$ . (See [BFM, Section 3.2] for a slight variant of this calculation.) Note that the subgroup of such triples is $2$ -dimensional, and therefore the associated homogeneous ${\check{{G}}}$ -space is $9-2=7$ -dimensional. Using that the ${\check{{G}}}$ -orbit of $\kappa(a^{2})$ is also $7$ -dimensional (e.g., by [GKZ, Example 4.5 in Chapter 14]), it is not hard to see from this calculation (by a limiting argument for $a\to 0$ ) that the stabilizer of the family $\kappa(\mathbf{A}^{1})\subseteq\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$ is precisely the claimed group scheme. ∎

This follows from the claim that $\mathrm{Spin}_{8}/\mathrm{G}_{2}\simeq S^{7}\times S^{7}$ . Perhaps the most “conceptual” way to see this is as follows. Using triality, one can identify $\mathrm{Spin}_{8}$ with the subgroup of $\mathrm{SO}_{8}^{\times 3}$ of those triples $(A_{1},A_{2},A_{3})$ such that $A_{1}(x_{1})A_{2}(x_{2})=A_{3}(x_{1}x_{2})$ for octonions $x_{1},x_{2}$ . Under this presentation, $\mathrm{G}_{2}$ corresponds to the subgroup where $A_{1}=A_{2}=A_{3}$ . The subgroups where $A_{1}=A_{3}$ (resp. $A_{2}=A_{3}$ ) are both isomorphic to $\mathrm{Spin}_{7}$ ; these are sometimes denoted $\mathrm{Spin}^{\pm}_{7}$ . The action of $\mathrm{Spin}_{8}$ on $S^{7}\times S^{7}$ sends $(x,y)\mapsto(A_{1}x,A_{2}y)$ ; one can check that this is transitive, and that the stabilizer of the point $(1,1)$ is precisely $\mathrm{Spin}^{+}_{7}\cap\mathrm{Spin}^{-}_{7}\cong\mathrm{G}_{2}$ .

That there is an equivalence $\mathrm{Spin}_{8}/\mathrm{G}_{2}\simeq S^{7}\times S^{7}$ at the level of cohomology with $\mathbf{Z}[1/2]$ -coefficients and mod $2$ coefficients, at least, is much simpler. On cohomology with $\mathbf{Z}[1/2]$ -coefficients, the map $\mathrm{G}_{2}\to\mathrm{Spin}_{8}$ is given by the map $\mathbf{Z}[1/2,p_{1},p_{2},p_{3},c_{4}]\to\mathbf{Z}[1/2,c_{2},c_{6}]$ sending

$$ x_{1}\mapsto 0,\ x_{2}\mapsto y_{1},\ x_{3}\mapsto y_{2},\ x_{4}\mapsto-(y_{1}+y_{2}). $$

The story in mod $2$ cohomology is similar. As described in [BFM], ${\check{{J}}}$ can be viewed as the group scheme over $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}\cong\spec\mathbf{Q}[y]$ of matrices of the form $g=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ by&a\end{pmatrix}$ with $\mathrm{det}(g)=a^{2}-b^{2}y=1$ . To understand ${\check{{J}}}[2]$ , note that $g^{2}=\begin{pmatrix}a^{2}+b^{2}y&2ab\\ 2aby&a^{2}+b^{2}y\end{pmatrix}$ , and since $2$ is a unit in $\mathbf{Q}$ , we find that $g$ is $2$ -torsion if and only if $ab=0$ and $a^{2}+b^{2}y=1$ . But since $\mathrm{det}(g)=1$ , this forces $a^{2}=1$ and $b=0$ . In other words, ${\check{{J}}}[2]$ is isomorphic to the constant group scheme $\mu_{2}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ . It follows that $(\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2})/{\check{{J}}}[2]\cong\mathrm{PGL}_{2}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ . No affine closure is necessary, since this is already affine. This suggests that there is a fully faithful functor from the $\infty$ -category of perfect complexes on a shearing of the $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ -quotient of $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ to $\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c}(G(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q})$ , i.e., a fully faithful functor

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{Perf}^{\mathrm{sh}}((\mathrm{PGL}_{2}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2})/\mathrm{SL}_{2}) \displaystyle\simeq\mathrm{Perf}^{\mathrm{sh}}(B\mu_{2}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2}) \displaystyle\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}^{c}(G(\!(t)\!)/\mathrm{PGL}_{2}(\!(t)\!);\mathbf{Q}). $$

This is the specialization of Conjecture 4.3 to the present case. Such a fully faithful functor does indeed exist: the inclusion of a basepoint of each of the two connected components of $G(\!(t)\!)$ corresponds to the inclusion of each of the two factors of $\mathrm{Perf}^{\mathrm{sh}}(B\mu_{2}\times\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}^{\mathrm{sh}}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/\mathrm{SL}_{2})^{\oplus 2}$ .

Let $n\geq 3$ , and let $V=\Sym^{n}(\mathrm{std})$ denote the $(n+1)$ -dimensional vector space of binary forms of degree $n$ , so that $V$ admits an action of $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ . Let $\kappa:\mathbf{A}^{1}/\!\!/(\mathbf{Z}/2)=\spec\mathbf{Q}[a^{2}]\to V$ denote the closed immersion sending

$$ a^{2}\mapsto\begin{cases}\frac{1}{2}((y+ax)^{n}+(y-ax)^{n})&n\text{ even};\\
\frac{1}{2a}((y+ax)^{n}-(y-ax)^{n})&n\text{ odd}.\end{cases} $$

A direct computation then shows that the stabilizer inside ${\check{{J}}}$ of $\kappa$ is isomorphic to ${\check{{J}}}[n]$ . Using the $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ -action on $V$ , one therefore obtains a map

$$ f:\overline{(\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times\mathbf{A}^{1})/{\check{{J}}}[n]}\to\Sym^{n}(\mathrm{std}). $$

When $n$ is odd, the vector space $\Sym^{n}(\mathrm{std})$ admits a symplectic structure: if we write $\sum_{j=0}^{n}\binom{n}{j}a_{j}x^{j}y^{n-j}$ for a general binary form of degree $n$ , the symplectic form (up to scaling) is given by

$$ \omega=\sum_{j=0}^{(n-1)/2}(-1)^{j}\binom{n}{j}da_{j}\wedge da_{n-j}. $$

Using this formula, one can check explicitly that the following diagram commutes:

$$ \textstyle{\overline{(\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times\mathbf{A}^{1})/{\check{{J}}}[n]}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{f} \textstyle{\Sym^{n}(\mathrm{std})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\mu} \textstyle{\overline{(\mathrm{SL}_{2}\times\mathbf{A}^{1})/{\check{{J}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\sim} \textstyle{\mathfrak{sl}_{2}^{\ast}.} $$

here, the vertical map is the moment map for $\Sym^{n}(\mathrm{std})$ . When $n=3$ , the map $f$ is an isomorphism by Proposition 4.8, but this will not be true for $n\geq 4$ . Indeed, $\kappa$ is generally not a section of an invariant-theoretic quotient map (see Remark 4.10)!

The above discussion has some consequences for global function fields. Let $\Sigma$ denote a smooth projective curve over $\mathbf{C}$ of genus $g$ . As described in [GR2], any symplectic ${\check{{G}}}$ -representation $V$ and a choice of square root $K_{\Sigma}^{1/2}$ of the canonical bundle of $\Sigma$ defines a Lagrangian substack $\mathcal{L}_{V}\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Higgs}_{{\check{{G}}}}(\Sigma)$ of the moduli stack of ${\check{{G}}}$ -Higgs bundles on $\Sigma$ . (One could more generally replace $V$ by a graded Hamiltonian ${\check{{G}}}$ -variety.) Roughly speaking, this Lagrangian substack consists of those Higgs bundles $(\mathcal{P},\theta)$ with $\theta\in\mathrm{H}^{0}(\Sigma;{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}_{\mathcal{P}}\otimes K_{\Sigma})$ obtained as the moment map image of a section of $V_{\mathcal{P}}\otimes K_{\Sigma}^{1/2}$ .

Proposition 4.8 and the above discussion together allow us to describe this Lagrangian explicitly when ${\check{{G}}}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ and $V=\Sym^{2n+1}(\mathrm{std})$ . Namely, the Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\Sym^{2n+1}(\mathrm{std})}\to\mathrm{Higgs}_{\mathrm{SL}_{2}}(\Sigma)$ fiberwise (over the Hitchin base) contains the $(2n+1)$ -torsion subgroup in the Prym variety; when $n=1$ , it is furthermore exactly the $3$ -torsion in the Prym variety. One can obtain similar descriptions for the other symplectic representations described in this article. For instance, Proposition 2.15 implies that if ${\check{{G}}}=\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}$ and $V=\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}$ , the Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{std}^{\otimes 3}}\to\mathrm{Higgs}_{\mathrm{SL}_{2}^{\times 3}}(\Sigma)$ is fiberwise (over the Hitchin base) given by the subgroup of the threefold product of the Prym variety consisting of those triples $(L_{1},L_{2},L_{3})$ of line bundles whose tensor product is trivial.
